propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes intermittent false-stall classification of dribbling fake remote despite test passing in isolation.
Delayed Python fixture wake-ups reduce actual throughput below promised rate, causing valid git transfers to appear stalled under the 2-second test window.
Cumulative bytes-owed catch-up alone is insufficient to prevent stall misclassification during uninterrupted scheduler gaps exceeding the configured window.
Test harness incorrectly applies the same 2-second artificial window to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls; production uses 10-second window.
Deterministic unit test of cumulative pacing math and split test windows (2s for stalls, 10s for integration with real Git) eliminate scheduler-sensitivity flakes.
